ref_extractions.title: Representation of symmetry in the extrastriate visual cortex from temporal integration of parts: An EEG/ERP study
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper investigates symmetry representation through temporal integration of occluded shapes using a different experimental paradigm. While it involves EEG and some overlapping authors (Makin, Bertamini, Rampone), it does not use or reference the openneuro_ds004347 dataset. The study examines object symmetry through dynamic occlusion, not the combined EEG/EMG symmetry classification task described in the dataset.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Different paradigm (occlusion integration); same research group but separate study not involving the dataset.

ref_extractions.title: Symmetry perception and affective responses: A combined EEG/EMG study
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper is the original source publication for the openneuro_ds004347 dataset. The title, authors (Makin, Wilton, Pecchinenda, Bertamini), paradigm (EEG/EMG symmetry perception), and experimental design (symmetry vs random patterns, 80 trials per condition) match the dataset description exactly. Authors are from University of Liverpool, same as dataset metadata.
ref_extractions.epoch_params: stimulus duration ~3s; focus on N1/P1 components and SPN
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Original publication for ds004347; combined EEG/EMG recording; participants classified reflection vs random patterns; experiments included 80 trials per condition; mentions Zygomaticus Major EMG activity alongside EEG.

ref_extractions.title: Sustained response to symmetry in extrastriate areas after stimulus offset: An EEG study
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper studies sustained SPN response after stimulus offset using a shape matching vs color task paradigm. While authors overlap (Bertamini, Rampone, Makin), it is a separate study investigating post-stimulus persistence of symmetry response. Not the same dataset or experimental design as ds004347.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Different experimental paradigm (stimulus offset, shape matching task); data availability not mentioned as OpenNeuro.

ref_extractions.title: Testing Whether and When Abstract Symmetric Patterns Produce Affective Responses
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper uses a behavioral priming paradigm (pattern-word interference task) to study affective responses to symmetry. It is NOT an EEG/EMG study—it uses reaction times and implicit measures only. No EEG data collection or OpenNeuro dataset involved.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Behavioral study using word classification task; no EEG/EMG recording; no dataset reference.

ref_extractions.title: The Pleasantness of Visual Symmetry: Always, Never or Sometimes
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper uses affective priming paradigm variants (4 experiments) to study when symmetry engenders positive affect. Like the other PLOS ONE paper, it is a behavioral study without EEG/EMG recording. References prior EEG work but does not use the openneuro_ds004347 dataset.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Behavioral affective priming experiments; no EEG data; different methodology from dataset.

ref_extractions.title: Electrophysiological priming effects demonstrate independence and overlap of visual regularity representations in the extrastriate cortex
ref_extractions.cot_reasoning: This paper uses EEG to study SPN priming effects across 5 experiments (48 participants each) investigating symmetry representation boundaries. Different paradigm (oddball detection, sequential pattern presentation) and separate data availability statement (OSF). Not the same dataset as openneuro_ds004347.
ref_extractions.evidence_desc: Different experimental design (sequential presentations, oddball task); 5 separate experiments with different participants; data on OSF not OpenNeuro.

feasibility_reason: The dataset has a well-documented paradigm from its original publication (symmetry vs random pattern classification), and despite lacking trial-level event markers in the EEG files, the analysis.md describes a viable approach using continuous segmentation with external metadata (stimulus timing files) to derive condition labels, supported by the relevant reference paper.

## Tasks

### Classical Task 1: Symmetry Perception Classification
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = -0.2 s, tmax = 0.8 s, baseline = [-0.2, 0.0]
- **Label Route**: `event`
- **Meta Level**: `raw`
- **Target Definition**:
  | Event | y | Meaning |
  |-------|---|---------|
  | `event_1` | 1 | Reflectional symmetry patterns (regular/symmetric) |
  | `event_3` | 0 | Random patterns (asymmetric) |
- **Evidence**:
  - DOI: `10.1016/j.neuropsychologia.2012.10.003` — Original publication; 80 trials per condition per participant; classifies symmetry vs random patterns; analyzes ERPs including N1/P1 components and stimulus-preceding negativity (SPN); combined EEG/EMG recording with 24 subjects.
- **Kernel Notes**: Event counts (event_1: 1920, event_3: 1919) align with ~80 trials × 24 subjects experimental design. Use `event_1`/`event_3` for trial-based epoching; exclude EMG/EOG channels (~10 channels) from the 73-channel set, retaining ~60-64 EEG channels. Verify polarity of event_1/event_3 mapping via DOI methodology if needed.

### Normal Task 1: Long Epoch Time-Frequency Analysis
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_long_event_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: tmin = -0.5 s, tmax = 2.0 s, baseline = [-0.5, -0.1]
- **Label Route**: `event`
- **Meta Level**: `raw`
- **Target Definition**:
  | Event | y | Meaning |
  |-------|---|---------|
  | `event_1` | 1 | Symmetry condition (long epoch for induced oscillations) |
  | `event_3` | 0 | Asymmetry condition (long epoch baseline) |
- **Evidence**:
  - DOI: `10.1016/j.neuropsychologia.2012.10.003` — Mentions SPN analysis requiring longer windows; supports time-frequency power analysis of symmetry perception; stimulus duration ~3s enables longer epoch capture of delta/theta oscillations.
- **Kernel Notes**: Longer 2.5s epochs enable better frequency resolution at lower bands (delta/theta). Use pre-stimulus baseline for normalization. Same channel exclusion applies (remove EMG/EOG).

### Potential Task 1: Continuous Segmentation with External Metadata
- **Task Type**: classification
- **Epoch Method**: `epoch_by_segmentation_hdf5`
- **Epoch Parameters**: segment_length = 2.0 s, overlap = 0.5 s
- **Label Route**: `event`
- **Meta Level**: `super`
- **Target Definition**:
  | Segment Condition | y | Meaning |
  |------------------|---|---------|
  | Pre-stimulus baseline | 0 | Window before stimulus onset from external timing logs |
  | Symmetry condition | 1 | Trials identified via stimulus timing files as symmetry |
  | Asymmetry condition | 2 | Trials identified via stimulus timing files as random |
- **Evidence**:
  - DOI: `10.1016/j.neuropsychologia.2012.10.003` — Supports condition-based labeling from experimental design logs; 80 trials per condition aligns with expected segment counts.
- **Kernel Notes**: Fallback approach if trial-level epoching is insufficient. Requires external metadata (stimulus timing/log files) to derive condition labels per segment. Apply sliding window across continuous recording, then merge condition labels from experimental design log.
